description: Implements Priority Based Budgeting for 2027 cycle.
Removes GHG additions from Climate Budget reporting.

chips.text: CFO Hack stated climate budgeting had little impact on decisions last cycle.
Partners or service providers may feel marginalized by lower priorities.
New climate action plan will integrate community adaptation and green infrastructure.
Administration will report on options for GHG emissions transparency.

description: Saskatoon transit ridership and land sales increased.
Citizen satisfaction with city services declined.
Greenhouse gas and waste diversion goals stalled.

chips.text: City Manager noted declining citizen satisfaction is a Canada-wide trend.
City hired first anti-advocate, hosted community feast and round dance.
Administration will explore partnering with Serita on indigenous procurement.

description: City implements new framework for managing $19 billion in assets.
Standardizes reporting to improve investment decisions and budgeting.
Initial reports on 10 asset categories begin mid-2025.

chips.text: Mayor Block noted new reporting helps council understand funding impacts.
Saskatoon residents benefit from improved asset management and services.

description: Board of Revision seeks two-year terms for members.

chips.text: Aligns Board of Revision terms with other city appeal boards.
Delegate flagged risk of undue influence on independent board through evaluation process.
Board committed to annual reports and evaluation summaries to Council.

description: Committee asks administration to report on Opimihaw Creek membership.

chips.text: Councillor Donauer questioned the benefit of Saskatoon joining the association.
The Opimihaw Creek Watershed Association seeks Saskatoon's membership.
Benefit of Saskatoon's involvement in the association remains unclear.
